rationale.complete: Round 1 done on 27 non-holdout periods (9 testable): card and dated predictions, synthetic validation on 4 real call schedules (7 worlds incl. the HH343 world, 40 runs; A1 fixed before data), replication with MH risk ratios, permutation null, K and channel sensitivities, pair strata, 3 natives (G51 post-read onset and phase sign, G44 arms, G42 descriptive), post hoc engagement control (A2), 70 estimate rows, frozen guarded confirm script (dry-run only).
rationale.faithfulness: HH343's prediction (2x departure after crossing co-switches, mutual 2-cycles, stronger in avoidance weeks) fails on every pre-registered test; the raw 1.15 excess disappears when chat engagement is matched (post hoc). The synthetic shows the Little-type read-gated model itself predicts RR < 1 at village sampling. C 1, D 0, E 0, F 1, H 0.
rationale.usefulness: A usable negative: update order does not cause thrashing on projects at village cadence, and true crossings are rare (1% of co-switches) because read-out takes ~20 s. Operators need not serialize claims. The touch-level outcome limits magnitude claims.

one_line: No 2-cycles: co-switch departures do not depend on who read whom once chat engagement is matched (RR 1.02); crossings are 1% of co-switches.

models.note: No Little 2-cycle; read-gated avoidance predicts RR < 1, observed 1.15 is engagement
Avoidance weeks (H93 J < 0) show no larger update-order effect

v2.claim: Agents who join the same project do not form 2-cycles: once chat engagement is matched, departures do not depend on who read whom (RR 1.02 [0.92, 1.13], 577 pairs); the raw 1.15× excess of unaware pairs is engagement, and true crossings are rare (1% of co-switches)
v2.scope: 9 testable periods, 2,227 co-switch pairs; natives G51, G44, G42

ladder.factor: synthetic on real call schedules (model predicts RR < 1)

v2.decision: don't worry about parallel-update oscillations in project choice
